To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ca2+ at low concentration replaces Mg2+ as a co-factor of the Ca2+ pump and that the Ca2+-pump is inhibited by high concentrations of Ca2+.

Ca2+ and Mg2+ act on the Ca2+ ATPase of red cell membranes by two different mechanisms, Ca2+ at concentrations below 1 microM acts as a transport ion and Mg2+ acts as an activator of phosphorylation and ATP hydrolysis.
the Ca2+-dependent ATPase from human red blood cell membranes requires Mg2+ to be activated and that Mg2+ acts at a site that is not the Ca2+-transport site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Ca and Mg on the phosphorylation reaction of the Ca-ATPase from red cells and the effects of Mg2+ on the Ca2+ transport reaction.
the effects of the divalent cations Mg2+ and Ca2+ at sites other than the transport site.
the role of Mg2+ as a modulator of the Ca2+ transport site in the Ca2+-activated ATPase from human red blood cell membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ca2+-dependent ATP hydrolysis is a two step process: the first step, the phosphorylation of the Ca2+ transport site, requires the presence of both Mg2+ and Ca2+, and the second step, the dephosphorylation, requires the presence only of Ca2+.
the effects of Ca and Mg on the phosphorylating activity and the ATPase activity are due to the action of these two cations at different sites of the Ca2+ pump.
the Ca2+-activated ATPase from human red blood cell membranes has two binding sites for Ca2+ and Mg2+, one at the transport site (Ca2+ site) and the other at an activating site (Mg2+ site).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mg2+ is required for the synthesis of E2P and for the E2P----E1P reaction but not for the E1----E1P and E1P----ADP+P reactions.
the Ca2+-transporting ATPase is a Mg2+ ATPase which is inhibited by Mg2+.
Mg2+ and Ca2+ are mutually exclusive at the transport site, that Mg2+ activates a reaction preceding phosphorylation and that Mg2+ accelerating the E1P--E2P reaction is inhibited by Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ca2+-dependent ATPase activity of the Ca2+ ATPase from red cell membranes is due to the presence of Mg2+ at the catalytic site of the enzyme and that the Ca2+ concentration required for half-maximal stimulation of the ATPase activity by Mg2+ (KCa) is 0.5 microM.
the Ca2+-transporting ATPase of red cell membranes is activated by Ca2+ at its transport site and by Mg2+ at a site distinct from the transport site.
the effects of Mg2+ on the phosphorylation reaction and the effects of Ca on the transport of Ca across the membrane are independent.
